subject: Subprocessor disclosure and KMS/HSM transfer clarification - PayBridge request
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@paybridge.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: LegalOps <legal@paybridge.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: current subprocessor roster + KMS/HSM locations

Hi Avery —

We're finalizing our procurement security review and need a complete list of Redwood's current subprocessors that touch customer data (processing or telemetry). In particular PayBridge's legal team wants:
- Full roster (name, country, processing role)
- Whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext customer content
- KMS/HSM provider and the physical location/jurisdiction where keys are stored
- Any cross-border transfers (APAC/EU/US) and whether there are onshore fallback options

Can you send the roster and a short attestation for KMS key custody by EOD Thursday PST? If you have a short summary PDF and anything for our procurement/LegalOps binder that would help.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Security, PayBridge
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@paybridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + KMS/HSM locations

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. We're compiling the roster now; attaching a current snapshot (subprocessor_roster_v20280329.pdf) and a short KMS/HSM attestation summary. Quick answers up front:
- KMS/HSM: primary key custody is with KeySafe HSM (managed customer key model). Primary key material is stored in US and EU HSM clusters; Redwood does not hand over raw vault keys to subprocessors.
- Plaintext access: most subprocessors only receive hashed/aggregated telemetry. A small set of onshore monitoring partners (listed in the roster) process logs that may include user-submitted content for debugging; those are bound by DPA clauses + additional NDA/processing restrictions.
- Cross-border transfers: our hosted offering routes by customer region; fallbacks may route through US/EU dedicated pools. For PayBridge specifically we can lock regionally if required.

Action items for us: Kimberly, can you confirm whether we should redact hostnames and internal VM IDs in the roster before sending to LegalOps? Ben, include the SOC2 summary and the DOC link.

I'll follow up with a DPA addendum DocuSign link for the explicit subprocessor clause and key custody language.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v20280329.pdf, kms_hsm_attestation_summary.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + KMS/HSM locations

Avery / Ben —

Quick legal/compliance notes for the outgoing packet to PayBridge:
- Redaction: redact internal hostnames and IPs (we can provide region + city-level location for data stores without naming internal resource ids).
- KMS disclosure: say "KeySafe HSM (US & EU regions) — Redwood maintains envelope keys; customer root keys are customer-managed when requested via Dedicated/Private deployments." Avoid publishing firmware versions or HSM serial numbers in a public doc.
- Plaintext access: be explicit about the small telemetry subset; recommend language: "Subprocessors only access plaintext data when explicitly required for debugging and under strict controls; such access is logged and subject to contractual restrictions."
- Provide a SOC2 summary and the redacted incident response contact.

I've attached a 1-page attestation snippet for KMS custody that Ben can fold into the packet.

Kimberly
General Counsel (Compliance) — Redwood Inference

On Thu, Mar 29, 2028 at 10:04 AM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the clear list. We're compiling the roster now; attaching a current snapshot ...

Thanks — that's helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement/LegalOps:
1) We need explicit confirmation whether any listed subprocessor has the technical ability to retrieve customer plaintext without an explicit API key from PayBridge (i.e., whether the subprocessors hold any decryption keys or services able to decrypt customer content).
2) For any subprocessors that do process plaintext for debugging, please include the last date when such access occurred (month/year) and a short justification.
3) If you can send the redacted roster + the KMS attestation as a single PDF and the DPA addendum DocuSign link, we'll route to our security committee.

If you can get that over by EOD your time we'll prioritize the review.

—Liam
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@paybridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-30T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: current subprocessor roster + KMS/HSM locations

Liam —

Appended the redacted roster and a combined attestation PDF (see attachments). Short answers to your numbered questions:
1) Decryption capability: None of our listed subprocessors hold customer master encryption keys. Operational helpers may process decrypted content only when PayBridge or another customer temporarily enables debugging access via token-based sessions; such sessions are time-limited, audited, and require a request approved by the customer's security contact.
2) Last plaintext-processing events: we included a month/year column in the roster for the three monitoring partners. All three show their last approved debug session during 2027-11 (Nov 2027) for discrete incident investigations. Each event entry includes a one-line justification.
3) DocuSign: here's the DPA addendum for your signature: https://app.docusign.com/rooms/PayBridge-DPA-Addendum-4321

Next steps: If LegalOps wants language stronger than the standard addendum (e.g., named onshore-only processing), Kimberly can coordinate the redline. If PayBridge needs a dedicated onshore-only routing policy we can scope Dedicated capacity timelines (2–4 weeks).

Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Avery
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
